subject: Acceleron multi-year stability exception request
messages:
From: Priya Sethi <priya@acceleron.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Jimenez <rafael.j@acceleron.ai>, procurement@acceleron.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for multi-year price stability (RFQ attached)

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the trial run last quarter — the team at Acceleron is ready to move forward but procurement has an ask we need your help with. They require a multi-year price stability commitment (price lock + renewal protection clause) as a condition of a 3-year committed spend.

High level:
- 3-year commitment starting Jan 1, 2027
- Request: price locked for first 24 months, then capped uplift for years 3 (max 8%)
- Renewal protection: ability to keep prices within X% of prior term unless material changes to spec/usage

This is time sensitive — our procurement team (cc'd) needs a partner-approved term sheet by end of week so legal can start their review. I attached our internal RFQ.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a stability clause like this and what the commercial constraints are?

Thanks,
Priya
Procurement Lead | Acceleron AI

Attachment: Acceleron_RFQ_Sept2026.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sethi <priya@acceleron.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for multi-year price stability (RFQ attached)

Hi Priya — appreciate the clear ask and timeline.

Short answer: we can support multi-year price stability in principle, but we need executive approval for a 24-month lock + capped uplift on year 3 because it departs from our standard uplift policy. I'm looping in Marissa (Sales), Markus (CRO), and Lauren (Legal/Sales Ops) to confirm constraints and sign-off cadence.

Next steps from our side:
- I'll attach a draft term sheet with an initial proposal (price lock for 24 months, year 3 uplift capped at 7%, renewal protection language tied to usage thresholds).
- Marissa/finance will run the impact calc and flag any guardrails (e.g., usage breakpoints, acceleration clauses).
- I'll come back with an ask to the execs if we need a one-time exception to standard escalation limits.

Marissa/Markus — can you review the attached draft and advise whether this is approvable under our current discount and risk tolerances? Also highlight any required mitigations (flooring mechanisms, minimum spend clauses).

Connor
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_term_sheet_v3.pdf, Acceleron_MAP_v2.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request for multi-year price stability (RFQ attached)

Thanks Connor — I reviewed the RFQ and the draft term sheet. Summary and recommendation below.

Summary of deal points (proposed):
- Term: 36 months (Jan 1, 2027 - Dec 31, 2029)
- Commitment: $3.6M ARR committed (phased ramp 12/12/12 months)
- Price lock: fixed unit price for months 1-24
- Uplift cap: max 7% Year-3 (compounded once at start of year 3)
- Renewal protection: automatic renewal at prior-term price +/- 3% unless usage growth > 30% or a material change in service tier
- Accelerators: overage rates to be billed at standard list rates; customer can convert to higher tier at ramp events

Why this is borderline:
- Locks + renewal protection remove our ability to reprice for market-driven cost changes; exposure grows if Acceleron's usage scales > forecast.
- Mitigations: include an annual usage review and a step-up clause if monthly usage exceeds forecast by >30% for >2 consecutive months. Also propose a one-time price true-up if aggregate usage exceeds committed baseline by >60% across any 12-month window.

Recommendation: Approve conditional exception to standard pricing policy provided we get signoff from finance and legal on the step-up/true-up language and add a minimum spend floor. Impacts attached in the finance calc.

If approved, I propose we offer the customer a 7% uplift cap (not 8%) with the mitigations above — that gives Acceleron the stability they want and reduces runaway exposure for us.

Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachment: finance_impact_calc_acceleron.xlsx

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Approval (conditional) — Acceleron stability exception

I reviewed Marissa's recommendation and the finance impact. Conditional approval granted. Conditions to be included in the term sheet before I sign:
- Include the 30% usage-trigger step-up clause and the 60% annual true-up floor that Marissa outlined.
- Add a carve-out for force majeure and for any required changes to comply with export/control rules.
- Add a clause that permits Redwood to migrate the customer to a compatible model variant if cost per token increases >20% due to upstream changes (this protects us against model-driven cost shocks).
- Legal (Lauren): confirm renewal protection language is clear and that renewals do not auto-extend price lock beyond year 2 without explicit sign-off.

Once those edits are in the term sheet and legal has given thumbs up, I authorize Connor to present this to Acceleron and circulate DocuSign.

Markus Klein
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference

On Wed, Sep 15, 2026 at 09:05 AM Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Markus — looping in Lauren for legal wording review.
>
> Connor

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sethi <priya@acceleron.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Acceleron multi-year terms (approved)

Hi Priya — good news. Redwood can commit to the stability package with the following agreed terms: 

Key agreed items (final):
- Term: 36 months (01/01/2027–12/31/2029)
- Commitment: $3.6M total committed spend
- Price lock: fixed unit price months 1–24
- Year-3 uplift: capped at 7% (compounded once at start of year 3)
- Renewal protection: renew at prior-term price +/- 3% unless usage growth >30% or material service changes; annual usage review required
- Usage trigger: >30% sustained growth for 2 consecutive months -> step-up dialogue; >60% aggregate annual overage -> one-time true-up at pre-agreed formula
- Carve-outs: force majeure, export/compliance, model-cost shock (we may migrate to compatible model variant if upstream cost changes >20%)

I've uploaded the revised term sheet and sent a DocuSign envelope for signature: https://docusign.com/1A2B3C/acceleron-term-sheet. Once signed we'll schedule a kickoff and enable the committed capacity.

Please confirm receipt and estimated e-sign date. If procurement wants edits to the renewal protection language please flag those and we'll route to legal immediately — we want to avoid last-minute redlines that delay Jan 1 start.

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_term_sheet_v4_for_acceleron.pdf (term sheet, redline resolved), Acceleron_MAP_v3.xlsx
